On the morning of June 24, information was received from Chief Inspector MacFarlene of Bubbling Well Station to the effect that the Chinese Police were interfering with the transportation of vegetables by hawkers coming from the Western suburbs at Keswick and Great Western Roads.

Enquiries made by Special Branch detectives reveal that the trouble was the result of dissension between the Western District Branch of the Central Wholesale Market at Brenan-Chungshan Roads U.O.L., and the Western Branch of the Shanghai Foodstuffs Market, 1365 Jessfield Road, U.O.L. The former is connected with the Shanghai City Government, while the latter is sponsored by Japanese. The Western Branch of the Shanghai Foodstuffs Market is reported to be carrying on more prosperous business than that of the Western District Branch of the Central Wholesale Market, consequently causing dissatisfaction.

On the morning of June 24, a number of vegetable hawkers, while passing Great Western and Brenan Roads, were warned by members of the Western District Branch of the Central Wholesale Market and Chinese police not to transport and sell their products to the Western Branch of the Shanghai Foodstuffs Market. C.D.S. 31. and the undersigned attended and the following was ascertained. 经侦探调查，查明若干受雇于日本人的中国称重员以受雇两个月仅收到一个月工资为由，于1940年5月28日上午拒绝工作。罢工显然是在市场开门营业且许多人已聚集买卖农产品后宣布的。由于无法称重，没有任何交易进行。负责市场的日本人下令关闭大门，此举得以执行，但随后商贩中似乎发生了骚乱，之后日本人指示重新打开大门，允许买卖双方离开。由于这一命令，大量商贩聚集在北西藏路上，造成了一定程度的阻碍。他们被劝往福建路桥市场，他们也照办了。未发生不幸事件。

March 19, 1940.                                      Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao (Kwang Hwa News Agency) :-

INAUGURATION OF PUPPET WESTERN DISTRICT MARKET UNLIKELY
IN NEAR FUTURE.

The inauguration of the so-called Central
Market which was originally arranged for the first part
of this month has been postponed. The construction of
the three-storey building of the new Western District
Market at the intersection of Brenan and Chung San Roads
has lately been completed and it is reported that its
inauguration will formally take place on March 25. A
committee of members has been formed to operate the market.
Chang Lung-hai (張龍海), the proprietor of the Chang
Kung Tai (張公泰) Native Products Hong, is the Chairman
of the committee. Chang Chao-kwei (張兆奎) of the
Tung Shing Hong (同興行), Sih Siao-ti (薛小弟) of
the Lu Shing Hong (祿興行) and Hsu Chien-chiu (許劍秋)
of the Lung Tai Hong (隆泰行) are members. Dealers
who are willing to participate in the market are required
to pay a charge of $800, first class, $400, second class
and $200, third class, as security.
At 10 a.m. yesterday the committee held
its inaugural meeting in the Yi Chia Tsung Restaurant
(一家春) at San Koo Chong (三用場), Zau Ka Doo.
The majority of the native products hongs in the Western
District are expressing their strong opposition to the
market and very few of them have taken part. The
report that the market will be inaugurated on a certain
date must therefore be treated with reserve.

Made by. and Forwarded by. Inspector S. V. Gash.

The inauguration ceremony in connection with the opening of the Shanghai Central Vegetable Market was held between 10a.m. and 12noon March 23. Appropriate arrangements were made in connection with the control of traffic in the vicinity.

September 28, 1939. Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Hwa Pao:

FORMATION OF A "VEGETABLE MART"

The Japanese and puppet authorities are tightening their control of the main food supplies of Shanghai.

It was learned yesterday that the "Vegetable Mart," which is being formed by the Shanghai City Government, is making preparations to transact business.

According to a vegetable dealer, in future a "registration fee" will be collected on vegetable coming to Shanghai from the suburbs, and on this account there will be a heavy increase in the price of vegetable. The formation of the mart is intended by the Japanese as a measure to accomplish their project for the control of the main food supplies in the Foreign Settlements of Shanghai.

It has been decided that the "Vegetable Mart" will be established at the former site of the Joint Savings Society Warehouse on North Soochow Road and that a jetty will be constructed so as to enable the vegetable supplies arriving by the Soochow Creek to be discharged there. In addition, a number of branch marts will be established in the suburbs.

According to a statement made by the Japanese, the enforcement of this measure of control will raise the value of vegetable consumed in Shanghai valued in the past at between $400,000 and $600,000 to approximately $1,000,000 per month.

Puppets' "Vegetable Market" To Open Soon
In Joint Savings Bank Godown In Chapei

Establishment Completes
Nippon Monopoly Over
Food Products Here

Sad news galore is in store for housewives in the foreign areas as the Japanese controlled "special Municipality of Greater Shanghai" prepares to throw open the doors of the "Shanghai Vegetable Market" for business.

Small traders peddling greens from Shanghai's surrounding country are in no happier mood because, it was asserted, they will have to follow the way of the meat dealers and the fish traders by paying a good share of their income to the puppet organization—all in the "holy name of a registration fee."

The operation of the "Vegetable Market" will complete the plans of the Japanese, trading circles revealed, of holding a monopoly over all the major food products consumed from day to day in the Concession and Settlement.

Meat Market Strike

When the fight broke out several months ago for the control of the meat trade in Shanghai, one informant recalled, it resulted for many days in the suspension of all meat business here. The price of pork at a time rose to nearly 92 cents a pound whereas the ordinary price level reached no higher than 30 to 40 cents.

Ironically enough, the new "Vegetable Market" will be located in the Soochow Creek godown of the Joint Savings Bank off the Yu Ya Ching Road bridge on Chapei side. The godown became internationally famous nearly two years ago when for five days the famed "Suicide Battalion" fought the Japanese troops, closing in on the building from three sides, for several days.

With the bank godown as headquarters, the "market" will set up branches all over the occupied areas in the vicinity of Shanghai. It will also incorporate under its wings several other wholesale markets already operating to supply Shanghailanders with vegetables. A Japanese report stated that the "market" will cost the puppet regime from ¥600,000 to ¥1,000,000, needed to provide the building with necessary loading facilities.

傀儡政权的“蔬菜市场”即将在闸北四行仓库开业

机构组建完成
日本在此垄断
食品产品

随着日本控制的“上海特别市”准备开放“上海蔬菜市场”进行营业，外国租界地区的家庭主妇们将面临诸多坏消息。

在上海周边乡村贩卖蔬菜的小商贩们心情同样不佳，因为据称，他们将不得不效仿肉商和鱼贩的做法，以“注册费”的神圣名义，向傀儡组织缴纳相当一部分收入。

商界人士透露，“蔬菜市场”的运营将完成日本人的计划，即对租界和公共租界日常消费的所有主要食品实行垄断。

肉类市场罢工

一位消息人士回忆说，几个月前为争夺上海肉类贸易控制权而爆发的斗争，导致这里所有的肉类生意停摆多日。当时猪肉价格涨至每磅近92美分，而正常价格水平不超过30至40美分。

具有讽刺意味的是，新的“蔬菜市场”将设在闸北一侧、虞洽卿路桥附近的苏州河四行仓库内。大约两年前，该仓库曾闻名国际，当时著名的“敢死队”（译者注：指谢晋元团）在该建筑内与日军激战五日，日军从三面包围该楼数天。

以银行仓库为总部，该“市场”将在上海附近的所有占领区设立分支机构。它还将把目前已运营的几个为上海外侨供应蔬菜的批发市场纳入其麾下。一份日本报告称，为该建筑提供必要的装卸设施，傀儡政权需花费60万至100万日元。

With the setting up of the "market" all vegetables formerly brought to the Settlement and Concession without the interference of the puppet regime, it was reported, will be diverted to the "market" or its branches. Peddlers To Be Affected
It will also seriously affect the small peddlers, they asserted, who will undoubtedly have greater difficulty in disposing of their goods and sell much less of them in point of quantity.
While regulations governing the "vegetable market" have not yet been announced, it is believed that they will follow the general pattern of the "Cattle Market" and the "Fish Market." In the latter puppet establishments, a special levy on the merchandise is made by the "special Municipality." In the "Meat Market," for instance, dealers are required to pay $2 on every pig they bring into the Settlement and Concession and fixed sums for cows, chicken, and ducks also.

预计价格上涨

据报道，随着“市场”的建立，以前未经傀儡政权干涉而运入租界和公共租界的所有蔬菜，都将被转运至该“市场”或其分支机构。商贩们认为，一旦“市场”开始运营，蔬菜价格肯定会达到前所未有的高位。

同一消息源透露，外国租界地区蔬菜成本的上升肯定会产生重大影响，正如大米价格上涨一样，因为这里绝大多数人的主食是大米和蔬菜，辅以极少量的肉类。

小贩将受影响

他们断言，这也将严重影响小商贩，他们无疑会在销售货物时面临更大困难，销量也会大幅减少。

虽然管理“蔬菜市场”的规定尚未公布，但据信其将遵循“牛市场”和“鱼市场”的一般模式。在这些傀儡机构中，“特别市”会对商品征收特别捐税。例如，在“肉类市场”，商贩每将一头猪运入租界和公共租界需缴纳2美元，牛、鸡和鸭也需缴纳固定金额。

Being Planned
Branches to Be Established
In Many Parts
Welcome news for Shanghai vegetarians and harassed housewives in these days of soaring food prices was contained in an announcement by the city fathers of Greater Shanghai that a central wholesale vegetable market to supply the needs of the Settlement, Concession, Pootung and Yangtsepoo will be opened soon under the supervision of the Special Municipality, the "Shanghai Mainichi" reported.

FRENCH POLICE INTELLIGENCE REPORT

Shanghai, August 18, 1939.

Farmers Sending Vegetables to French Concession Interfered with
During the past few days, Japanese merchants coming
from Hongkew have been compelling farmers on Hungjao Road, which
lies beyond the French military zone at Zikawei, to sell their
vegetables to them at reduced prices. These vegetables were
being taken by the farmers to the French Zone for sale.
Farmers who refused to sell to the Japanese were often maltreated
by the Japanese and their vegetables were confiscated. Owing to
this, reduced supplies of vegetables are entering the French
Military Zone at Zikawei.

Book-Binders Form Union
A dozen book-binders have formed a union with an
office at House No. 6 Lane 109, Canton Road. They are trying
to secure members. They will collect a fee of $1.00 each
every month.
It will be recalled that recently some 800 book-
binders went on strike for more pay and satisfaction was given
them by the employers.

上海，1939年8月18日。

向法租界运送蔬菜的农民受到干扰
在过去几天里，来自虹口的日本商人一直在迫使位于徐家汇法国军事区以外虹桥路上的农民以低价向他们出售蔬菜。这些蔬菜本是农民运往法租界销售的。拒绝向日本人出售的农民经常遭到日本人的虐待，他们的蔬菜也被没收。因此，进入徐家汇法国军事区的蔬菜供应量减少。

装订工成立工会
十多名装订工在广东路109弄6号成立了一个工会。他们正在努力招募会员。他们将每人每月收取1.00美元的费用。
记得最近约有800名装订工为要求加薪而罢工，雇主满足了他们的要求。

FRENCH POLICE INTELLIGENCE REPORT

Shanghai, August 21, 1939.

Italian Marines Search Houses
At about 9 a.m. August 19, nine Italian marines carried out a search for arms and ammunition among the houses in Kang Foh Li, Lane 22, Brenan Road (extra-Settlement road). The search lasted until 10 a.m. but nothing was found.
In this lane there are numerous opium and smoking dens and morphine selling hongs.

Pay of Garbage Removal Coolies Increased.
The Chu Cheng Kee Co., located in Room 318 of the Chung Wei Building, No. 16 Rue Porte du Nord, undertakes the removal of garbage from the French Concession. It employs 200 boatmen, pontoon coolies etc. whose wages range from $15 to $20 a month.
Owing to the high cost of living, the company has informed the workers that their wages will be increased by 20% as soon as the removal of garbage from the French Concession to Pootung has been resumed.
In the meantime, the coolies are being paid only 50% of their wages. It is said that work will be resumed very soon.

上海，1939年8月21日。

意大利海军陆战队搜查房屋
8月19日上午9时许，九名意大利海军陆战队员在布伦安路（越界筑路）22弄康福里（Kang Foh Li）的住户中搜查武器和弹药。搜查持续至上午10时，但一无所获。
该弄堂内有许多鸦片烟馆、吸烟所以及吗啡售卖商号。

清道夫工资增加。
位于北门外大街16号众维大楼318室的朱成记公司（Chu Cheng Kee Co.）承包法租界的垃圾清运工作。该公司雇佣船夫、驳船苦力等200人，月薪在15至20元之间。
由于生活成本高昂，公司已通知工人，一旦恢复将垃圾从法租界运往浦东的工作，他们的工资将增加20%。
在此期间，苦力们仅领取50%的工资。据悉，工作很快将恢复。

某些邮政职员的活动。
一名叫蒋平兴（Chiang Ping Shing）的邮差，在最近的加薪运动中表现活跃，已接到命令前往杭州就任新职。他试图获得邮政局长的许可，让另一名他曾承诺给予一定报酬的邮差代替他去杭州任职，但其请求被驳回。

Vegetable Supplies.

This morning (August 21) policemen of the Shanghai

vegetables had first to be sent to the mart in Hongkew.

Several dealers succeeded in sending their wares
direct to Marche de l'Est where 600 baskets were landed.

The Ricsha Hire Charge.

Besides the ricshas provided with S.M.C. licences
about 6,500 ricshas carrying only French Concession licenses
are operating in the French Concession. The hire charge for
these vehicles ranges from 35 cents to 40 cents a day (from
5 a.m. to midnight).

Owing to the high cost of materials used in the
construction of ricshas, the Ricsha Owners Association, at the
request of members, has issued a notice to ricsha coolies on
August 19 informing them that as from August 20 the hire
charge would be raised to 42 cents per vehicle per diem.

On August 13, the Japanese authorities in
Pootung issued a notice to the effect that as from
August 16, 1939, the vegetable market in Pootung

Settlement and French Concession. However, as the

Dazang which are put on sale in Hongkew. The vegetable
dealers at the French Bund depend principally upon
supplies from Hangchow and other places in the interior,
while those dealers in the Settlement receive the greater
part of their supplies from the interior which arrive

DIFFICULTY TO CONTROL VEGETABLE MARKET

In an attempt to gain control of the
vegetable market, the Japanese have ordered that
vegetables from Pootung should be marketed in Hongkew,
notices to this effect having been posted up in Pootung.
It is learned that this measure was suggested by
a young Japanese in connivance with villagers with a
view to making money.
Though the Japanese naval authorities in
Pootung have approved this measure, the Japanese
authorities in Hongkew have refused to give sanction
to the matter, fearing that undesirable elements might
enter Hongkew in the disguise of vegetable vendors.
However, secret arrangements are being made to bring
the matter under control.

控制菜市场的困难

为了试图控制菜市场，日本人下令
浦东的蔬菜必须在虹口上市，相关
告示已在浦东张贴。
据悉，这一措施是由一名年轻日本人与
村民串通提出的，目的是牟利。
虽然浦东的日本海军当局已批准
这一措施，但虹口的日本当局拒绝
批准此事，担心不良分子可能伪装成
菜贩进入虹口。
不过，正在秘密安排以将该事项纳入
管制之下。

August 16, 1939. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and Chinese-American Daily News :-

JAPANESE CONTROL OVER TRANSPORTATION OF VEGETABLES IS
DIRECTED AGAINST THE FOREIGN SETTLEMENTS

The Japanese control over the transportation
of vegetables comes into effect as from to-day. No
vegetables will be allowed to enter the Foreign Settlements
by way of the Tung Chong Road jetty. Hereafter, peasants
must take their vegetables to the Hongkew Market by way
of the Chi Chong Wharf. Consequently all vegetable hawkers
in the Foreign Settlements will have to make their purchases
from Hongkew. It is generally believed that during the
first few days of the enforcement of this control, the
price of vegetables will not be increased in order to draw
more business. However, as soon as everything is going
on smoothly, an increase in prices will be made.
It is said that this measure is being taken
by the Japanese as a move against the Settlements; it will
not be applied in the suburbs of this city.

Market in Hongkew will control all transactions in fruits
and vegetables and all farmers who bring vegetables every
day to the Foreign Settlements for sale are required to
use the ferry boats from the Chi Chong Wharf, Pootung, to
take their produce to the Fruit and Vegetable Market in
Hongkew. As Settlement vegetable hawkers have to go to
Hongkew to buy vegetables, there will be no more Pootung
vegetable sellers in the markets in the Foreign Settlements.
The Chi Chong Wharf ferry service is operated by the Nisshin
Kisen Kaisha. Already the prices of vegetables have gone
up considerably.
At present, Japanese are controlling food
supplies at Me Sz Doo and Tsingpu, while the Livestock

Shun Pao and Sin Wan Pao :- 17.8.39 (AM)

JAPANESE AND VEGETABLES FOR THE SETTLEMENTS

Recently the Japanese authorities posted up
in Pootung copies of a circular notice to the effect that
commencing from August 16 all vegetables are to be taken
to Hongkew for sale.
Enquiries made show that for reasons unknown
this new measure was not put into force yesterday and no
notice of a postponement of the enforcement of this new
measure has been issued.
As a result, a large number of vegetable
hawkers could be seen moving about in uncertainty along the
Pootung Highway yesterday morning. Some seemed to be going
to the Chi Chong Wharf, while others went to the Tung Chong
Road Jetty. Later all were allowed by the puppet Police
Bureau to board ferry boats with their wares to be taken
into the Foreign Settlements.
For this reason there was no shortage of
vegetables in the various markets yesterday.

日本人与供往租界的蔬菜

近日，日本当局在浦东张贴了
通令副本，称自8月16日起，所有蔬菜
须运往虹口出售。
经查询显示，出于未知原因，
这一新措施昨天并未实施，也未发布
推迟实施该新措施的通告。
结果，昨天上午可以看到大量蔬菜
小贩在浦东公路上犹豫不决地走动。有些人似乎
正前往其昌码头，而另一些人则前往
通中路码头。后来，伪警察局允许所有人
携带货物登上渡轮，运入
外国租界。
因此，昨天各个市场并未出现
蔬菜短缺。

JAPANESE CONTROL VEGETABLES TRADE IN POOTUNG

Shanghai receives supplies of vegetables and
fruits from Pootung, Zi Ka Wei, Poh Sin Kyung, Huang Tu
and Hangchow.
On August 13, a notice was posted up in the
Vegetable Market in Pootung to the effect that all
vegetables in Pootung will be placed under the control of
the market. This will seriously affect the livelihood of
4000 persons engaged in this business. Shanghai buys from
Pootung over $400,000 worth of vegetables every year.
In normal times, the vegetables are transported
here via Tung Ka Tu (董家渡) and Pootung Point. There
will be no shortage of vegetables, but the price will
certainly go up.
The notice mentioned above reads as follows:-
"The public is hereby notified that the market
has been instructed by General Yamasaki, with the approval
of the Japanese Naval Special Landing Party at Pootung, to
undertake the transportation of vegetables from Pootung
to Hongkew via the Chi Chong Wharf (其昌碼頭). This will
take effect as from August 16, 1939. Enquiries may be made
at the provisional office of this market at No. 334 Chi
Chong Street (其昌棧街)."

Subject Ferry Service between Shanghai and Pootung.

Made by D. S. Hocking Forwarded by C. Crawford D. I

The tugs "Diana Moller" and "Minnie Moller" operating
as ferries to Pootung, have, in the past two weeks, been
stopped several times by Japanese. On November 30, three
Japanese, described as soldiers, boarded the "Minnie Moller"
and after searching passengers and members of the crew,
decamped with some $200.00 fare money and ten books of tickets.
Again on December 3, the tug "Diana Moller" when passing
Tungkeu was forced to stop by a shot fired from a Japanese
naval launch, following which the tug was ordered to Kaochiao
and the passengers driven ashore. Military officers boarded
the ship and after a thorough search left with $900.00
ticket money and various books and ticket-stubs.

In reply to complaints made by Moller & Co. to the Japanese
Consulate-General, they have been informed that such high-
handed action on the part of Japanese naval and military
representatives is not sanctioned by the authorities nor
will it be permitted in future. Moller & Co. were further
advised that any ship other than Japanese, approaching
Tsungming Island, will be fired upon without question and
that any unauthorised persons or boats landing at Tungkeu
or in the immediate vicinity will be detained. It is
understood that Tungkeu has been turned into a temporary
base by the Japanese for stores and munitions.

The ferry service at the present date is operating
normally.

At about 12.30 p.m. on November 29, the "Diana Moller",
whilst on her regular downstream run to Gough Island was
stopped in mid-stream and boarded by several Japanese in
uniform. An overbearing attitude was adopted towards the
captain and he was told that his passengers would not be
permitted to land in Pootung and to return to Shanghai. This
he did and reported to the office whereat a strong verbal
protest was registered by Moller & Co. with the Japanese
Consulate-General and a letter relating the facts of the
incident sent to H.B.M. Consulate. Another trip to Gough
Island was made later the same afternoon, the return journey
with vegetables being completed without incident.

Permingeat & Cie, operating a similar service to that
of Moller & Co. have also met with difficulties as embodied
in the attached miscellaneous report. On this occasion an
employee of the company, Mr. Gisdakis, of Greek nationality,
was removed from the launch at Pootung by Japanese officers
and held throughout the day, reportedly being subjected to
continued threats and abuse while being detained. He was
released in Yangtszepoo District and made his way back to
the Settlement, arriving at about 9 p.m. after having had to
apply to the Japanese Consulate-General for a pass to cross
the Garden Bridge. Permingeat & Cie. made no protest over
the incident but state that they have since concluded arrange-
ments with Japanese officials whereby the ferry service will
meet with no further hindrance.

Setting an example to other administrative bodies in Shanghai, the Japanese Residents' Corporation has gone into the vegetable business, the Shanghai "United News" reported yesterday.

With Hongkew facing a vegetable famine, the Corporation, which governs the local Japanese community, took determined steps to alleviate the situation.

Agents were sent to Pootung to purchase greens from farmers. Ferried across the river, the vegetables were then sold by the Corporation's salesmen at the Hongkew Market.

Prices Of Food
Sky-rocket Here

Vegetables, All Meat,
Eggs, Fish Climb
To New Highs

Despite encouraging messages of cheer from the authorities to the effect that soon the state of emergency as regards food will be no more, local housewives are facing the very present problem of leaping prices on local foodstuffs markets. Prices are still rocketing to heights unattained since the start of hostilities, this scaling of peak rates being especially noticeable in vegetables. Vegetarians are being forced to subdue their tastes now, as increases upto 200 per cent are noted in the past week above and beside the raises that were in force before that seven-day period of elevation. Bamboo shoots are today 45 cents per pound instead of 30, French beans are 50 instead of 20-25 cents per pound, beetroots now sell at 30 cents the pound whereas one week ago they were only 10 cents. Cabbage, endives, garlic, lettuce, onions, potatoes and turnips have all gone up 100 per cent or more, while celery, carrots, ginger, green pepper, leeks, parsnips, pumpkin, spinach and tomatoes have also increased greatly.

Fruit Steady

The report issued by the S.M.C. Superintendent of Food, Markets and Bakeries notes only one division of foodstuffs that has remained steady in the midst of the general rise. Fruits are for the most part available at prices in force a week and more ago, and Chinese oranges and Amoy pumelos have even decreased five cents.

This is more than made up for, however, by butcher's meats. Here, pork has gone up to 50-70 cents per pound, while beef is 40-60 cents. Veal has risen to 55-90 cents, and even mutton has undergone an increase to 35-80 cents per pound. Wild duck, in the game division, are now 70 cents each, while woodcocks are 50 cents and snipe 25 cents each.

Poultry High

On the poultry mart, spring chickens are extinct at present,

(Concluded from Page 1)
while ducks are 70-$1.50 each, and their eggs 80 cents per dozen. Fowl are now 50 cents per pound, and chickens' eggs are 45-60 cents per dozen. Geese have risen to $2.50 each. In the meantime, and pigeons are 20 cents instead of 25 cents. Rabbit, teal and venison have gone off the market.

The fish market now appears to be on its last legs, as only pomfret, whitebait and yellow fish at steady prices, and soles at 25-20 cents per pound remain. Meanwhile, Shanghai flour is $4.00 per 50 pounds, while rice is no longer sold in 200-pound bags, but can only cost nine cents.

Fuel, keeping pace with the other items listed, has also gone up the price scale. Best anthracite is $25 per metric ton day, while No. 1 house coal is $30 and No. 1 kitchen coal is down $2 to come up to the same level.

While a Japanese spokesman late this morning denied knowledge of negotiations between the Shanghai Municipal Council and the Japanese authorities vis-a-vis the present food situation, an official of the S.M.C. reaffirmed that these negotiations were progressing. The arrangements sought by the Council are those whereby Chinese farmers bringing vegetable to the Settlement and Concession would be allowed to go back to their farms in Pootung and the western district to bring back more supplies to Shanghai. If required, the S.M.C. official declared, escorts will be provided for these trips.

Although "wartime prices" are still in force for foods, with the conclusion of the hostilities in the immediate vicinity of Shanghai, it is understood from the authorities that very likely the prices will in the near future descend to more normal levels.

Hoarding of food-stuffs, profiteering by unscrupulous provision store-keepers and genuine scarcity have combined to raise the prices on the local market to height not scaled even during the time that the hostilities were being waged close by. The recent encirclement of Shanghai by the Japanese forces has, however, closed Pootung and the southern and western districts and these have caused the present state of affairs.

Towards Decline

In the last few days, especially yesterday, the trend of prices could be noticed straining towards a decline as the Japanese permitted farmers to come into Shanghai with their vegetables, only foodstuffs still obtainable close to Shanghai. However, the situation is not greatly eased because the farmers that enter Shanghai's foreign areas are not allowed back to their farms again, and this impedes a steady flow of food into the Settlement and Concession.

It is this condition that the S.M.C. was trying yesterday to combat, and negotiations were going on this morning with the Japanese authorities to permit Chinese soil-tillers to return to their farms and continue a regular transport of vegetables to the foreign districts. It is pointed out that prices were already from 30 to 40 per cent higher than usual, and a shortage is noticeable enough without restricting liberties in those few areas not too hard hit by the hostilities.

Meat Serious

The situation as regards meat is also rather serious, but the S.M.C. notes that it is not as bad as viewed generally. The sources of Shanghai's meat supplies are for the most part involved in the conflict which has shifted to the north, south and west. But nevertheless the authorities of both Settlement and Concession do not feel great concern over this problem as there are still emergency supplies in Hongkew, and these are not yet called for.

While foreigners are chiefly aware of the great increase in prices of vegetables and meats, which it is understood will soon decrease as the improvement in shipping schedules aids in abolishing shortages, local Chinese are concerned with their staple food, rice, and its price increases. However, this question was studied and as a result the S. M. C. is in the position of having adequate supplies on hand, with more shipments ready in case of a lasting emergency.

食品价格
在此飞涨

蔬菜、各类肉类、
鸡蛋、鱼类价格
攀升至新高

尽管当局发出令人鼓舞的安慰消息，称有关食品的紧急状态即将结束，但本地家庭主妇们正面临着本地食品市场价格飙升这一迫在眉睫的问题。价格仍在飙升至自战事开始以来未曾达到的高度，这种峰值的攀升在蔬菜方面尤为明显。素食者现在被迫克制他们的口味，因为在过去的一周里，除了此前七天上涨期已经实行的涨幅之外，又记录了高达 200% 的增幅。竹笋今天每磅 45 分，而不是 30 分；四季豆每磅 50 分，而不是 20-25 分；甜菜根现在每磅售价 30 分，而一周前仅为 10 分。卷心菜、菊苣、大蒜、生菜、洋葱、土豆和芜菁都上涨了 100% 或更多，而芹菜、胡萝卜、姜、青椒、韭葱、欧防风、南瓜、菠菜和西红柿也大幅上涨。

水果价格稳定

由工部局食品、市场和面包房主管发布的报告指出，在普遍上涨中，只有一个食品类别保持稳定。水果大部分仍按一周多以前的现行价格供应，而且中国柑橘和厦门柚子的价格甚至下降了五分。

然而，屠夫销售的肉类完全抵消了这一稳定局面。在此，猪肉已涨至每磅 50-70 分，牛肉为 40-60 分。小牛肉涨至 55-90 分，甚至羊肉也涨至每磅 35-80 分。野味类中的野鸭现在每只 70 分，丘鹬每只 50 分，沙锥鸟每只 25 分。

家禽价格高企

在家禽市场上，童子鸡目前绝迹，

（接第 1 版）
而鸭子每只 70 分至 1.50 美元，鸭蛋每打 80 分。家禽肉现在每磅 50 分，鸡蛋每打 45-60 分。鹅已涨至每只 2.50 美元。同时，鸽子价格为 20 分，而非 25 分。兔子、茶色野鸭和鹿肉已退出市场。

鱼市现在似乎已奄奄一息，因为只有鲳鱼、银鱼和黄鱼价格稳定，以及比目鱼保持在每磅 20-25 分。与此同时，上海面粉每 50 磅 4.00 美元，而大米不再以 200 磅一袋出售，只能以每（单位不明，原文如此）九分的价格购买。

燃料与其他列出的项目保持同步，价格也呈上升趋势。最好的无烟煤每天每公吨 25 美元，而一号家用煤为 30 美元，一号厨房用煤则下降 2 美元以达到相同水平。

虽然一位日本发言人今天上午晚些时候否认知晓工部局与日本当局之间就当前食品局势进行的谈判，但工部局的一位官员重申，这些谈判正在进行中。工部局寻求的安排是，允许将蔬菜运入租界和法租界的华农返回浦东和西区，以便向上海带回更多物资。工部局官员宣称，如有需要，将为这些行程提供护卫。

虽然食品仍维持“战时价格”，但随着上海附近地区战事的结束，据当局透露，价格很可能在不久的将来降至更正常的水平。

囤积食品、无良杂货店主的牟取暴利以及真正的短缺，共同导致本地市场价格上涨至甚至在附近发生战事期间都未曾达到的高度。然而，日军最近对上海的包围封锁了浦东以及南部和西部地区，这造成了目前的局势。

趋向下跌

在最近几天，特别是昨天，可以注意到价格趋势倾向于下跌，因为日本人允许农民带着蔬菜进入上海，这些是上海附近仅能获得的食品。然而，局势并未得到极大缓解，因为进入上海外国区域的农民不被允许再次返回他们的农场，这阻碍了食品持续流入公共租界和法租界。

工部局昨天正试图对抗这种状况，今天上午正与日本当局进行谈判，以允许中国耕种者返回农场并继续向外国区域定期运输蔬菜。有人指出，价格已经比平时高出 30% 到 40%，即使不限制那些受战事影响不太严重的少数地区的自由，短缺现象也已经足够明显。

肉类形势严峻

肉类方面的形势也相当严峻，但工部局指出，情况并不像普遍认为的那样糟糕。上海肉类供应的来源大多卷入已转移至北、南和西部的冲突中。尽管如此，租界和法租界的当局对此问题并不感到过分担忧，因为虹口仍有应急储备，且尚未被调用。

虽然外国人主要意识到蔬菜和肉类价格的大幅上涨——据悉随着航运时刻表的改善有助于消除短缺，这些价格很快将下降——但本地中国人关心的是他们的主食大米及其价格上涨。然而，这个问题已得到研究，结果是工部局手头有充足的供应，并在发生持久紧急情况时准备有更多的装运货物。

Food Stuffs
To Be Brought
From Pootung

Farmers Of Peninsula
Given Permission Of
Ingress And Egress

A general improvement in Shang-
hai's food situation was fore-
shadowed yesterday as a result of
a series of important developments
brought about as a result of the
arrangements made by the Shang-
hai Municipal Council.
These developments, which are
likely to result in lower prices and
more abundant supplies, are:
Arrangement made by the S.M.C.
with the Japanese authorities, which
will permit farmers to return to
Pootung to bring vegetables to
Shanghai;
Plans for bringing live hogs to
the city from Nantungchow, with
the first shipment slated to arrive
in the next two days; and the
import of vegetables from Tsing-
tao, with the first consignment
scheduled to reach the city within
the week.

Agreement Secured

Permission from the Japanese
which enables the farmers to make
regular trips to and from Pootung
was secured by the Council on Mon-
day. Two tugs of the Moller
Company have been secured to
ferry the truck gardeners and these
will make two trips daily, carrying
some 700 persons on each trip.
Garden produce, which is expected
considerably to increase local sup-
plies, will be brought over from
the Koochiao area.
Since the Japanese occupation of
the areas outside the Settlement
and the Concession, farmers from
Pootung were only allowed to come
to Shanghai, but were not permitted
to return to their farms. As a re-
sult, there was a diminishing sup-
ply, as Pootung is now the chief
source for fresh greens for local
markets. The new arrangements, it
is understood, are being carried
out satisfactorily, as a large num-
ber of farmers and dealers are al-
ready making use of the tugs for
transporting their vegetables.

A Council official in charge of
the food arrangements told the re-
porter that a general survey of
various markets yesterday morning
showed that there was a definite
increase in vegetables which were
scarce during the last few days, while
prices in many instances showed
decreases.

Hogs Coming

Butchers in the Settlement and
the Concession have also completed
plans for sending regular ships to
Nantungchow to secure live hogs.
It was learned yesterday that
several boatloads are slated to
arrive either today or tomorrow.
Additional supplies will be brought
to Shanghai. In this case, as in
other food supply problems the
Council aided the merchants in
securing the necessary permits.

Further increasing the local
Saigon rice supply, some 20,000 bags
of the grain of 220 pounds each
are slated to arrive here during the
week-end. The boat, delayed by
typhoon, was originally due here on
Friday.

N.S. Hwang

《字林西报》 1937年11月10日
276-8

食品
将从浦东
运入

半岛农民
获准进出

由于工部局所作安排带来的一系列重要发展，上海食品局势的总体改善在昨天已现端倪。
这些可能带来更低价格和更充足供应的发展包括：
工部局与日本当局达成的安排，允许农民返回浦东将蔬菜运往上海；
从南通州将活猪运入城市的计划，第一批货物预计在未来两天内抵达；以及从青岛进口蔬菜，第一批货物计划在本周内抵达本市。

达成协议

工部局于周一获得了日本人的许可，使农民能够定期往返浦东。莫勒公司（Moller Company）的两艘拖轮已被征用以摆渡菜农，这些拖轮每天航行两次，每次运送约 700 人。预计将大幅增加本地供应的园艺产品将从顾家宅（Koochiao）地区运来。
自从日军占领租界和法租界以外的地区以来，浦东农民只被允许来上海，但不被允许返回他们的农场。结果，供应逐渐减少，因为浦东现在是本地市场新鲜绿叶蔬菜的主要来源。据了解，新的安排正在顺利执行，因为大量农民和商贩已经利用拖轮运输他们的蔬菜。

一位负责食品安排的工部局官员告诉记者，昨天上午对各个市场的全面调查显示，前几天稀缺的蔬菜数量明显增加，而在许多情况下价格显示下降。

生猪将至

租界和法租界的屠夫们也完成了派遣定期船只前往南通州获取活猪的计划。昨天获悉，几船货物计划于今天或明天抵达。额外的供应将被运往上海。在这种情况下，如同其他食品供应问题一样，工部局协助商人获得了必要的许可证。

为进一步增加本地西贡大米的供应，约 20,000 袋每袋 220 磅的大米计划在本周末抵达此处。该船因台风延误，原定于周五抵达。

N.S. Hwang
C.S.
